# Chapter 4: Methodology

## 3.1 Python Environment for Machine Learning

The system is built entirely on Python 3.14.3. The core machine learning stack includes sentence-transformers for embedding representation, FlagEmbedding for BGE-M3 model utilities and ColBERT score calculation, pinecone-client for serverless vector database operations, motor for asynchronous MongoDB connection, langchain-text-splitters for recursive chunking, and chainlit for the user interface.

## 3.2 Platform and Machine Configurations

The system was developed and tested on a macOS workstation. Local execution uses Apple Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) via PyTorch to accelerate embedding model inference. Production vector storage is deployed on Pinecone's serverless cloud infrastructure (us-east-1). Conversations are persisted in a local MongoDB database instance (v7.0) running asynchronously. LLM generation runs on Groq's high-speed LPU (Language Processing Unit) cloud API.

## 3.3 Data Split and Processing

The system targets the HotpotQA training set. To build the vector store, 200 records are preprocessed, yielding 649 gold documents. The context text is split into chunks of 512 characters with an overlap of 50 characters. This aligns chunks with ground-truth facts while the overlap ensures that bridge entities linking two facts are not cut in half.

## 3.4 Model Planning

The model pipeline is divided into three layers: (1) Embedding: BAAI/bge-m3, a multilingual, multi-functional model producing 1024-dimensional dense vectors and lexical weights. (2) Re-ranking: BGE-M3 ColBERT late-interaction scoring. (3) Generation: Groq llama-3.3-70b-versatile, with fallback to llama-3.1-8b-instant and gemma2-9b-it on rate limits.

## 3.5 Model Training and Vector Indexing

Vector store indexing is executed by the ingestion pipeline. Raw JSON records are loaded, distractor paragraphs are discarded, and gold paragraphs are chunked. For each chunk, the Embedder generates dense vectors and sparse lexical weights. These are uploaded to Pinecone in batches of 100 vectors, using a dotproduct distance metric.

## 3.6 Model Evaluation and Optimization

Retrieval is evaluated on 50 synthetic test queries using Hit Rate, Recall, Precision, MRR, and NDCG. Generation is evaluated using a Gemini-as-a-judge framework with RAGAS metrics (Faithfulness, Answer Relevancy, Context Recall, Context Precision, and Answer Correctness). Optimization involved tuning the hybrid alpha weight (settling on alpha=0.2 dense and 0.8 sparse) and refining prompt guidelines to prevent the generator from inserting inline bracketed citations into the final answer.
